 LM KR Lisa Monica, Kholid Rafsanjani 01 November 2026, 11:00 WIB LM Lisa Monica Reporter KR Kholid Rafsanjani Reporter WhatsApp Channel Bahlil suspects Singapore resold 148 Indonesian LNG cargoes abroad. JAKARTA - Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Regional Development? No. Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Downstreaming and Energy Transition, Bahlil Lahadalia, suspects that Singapore has been reselling some of the liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplied by Indonesia to other countries.
 Bahlil, who also serves as Energy and Mineral Resources Minister, said Indonesia had exported up to 409.5 million standard cubic feet per day (MMSCFD) of natural gas to Singapore. The entire volume was delivered through pipelines from Natuna and mainland Sumatra.
 In addition to natural gas, Bahlil said Indonesia had also exported 1,480 million standard cubic feet (MMSCF), equivalent to 148 LNG cargoes.
 "However, I believe that not all 148 cargoes were used for Singapore's domestic needs. Some were traded and subsequently re-exported to other countries," Bahlil said during a press briefing at the State Palace in Jakarta several days ago.
 Read Also: November foreign trade opens with Rp375 billion outflow In response to the allegation, the Singapore government issued a statement.
 Singapore's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (MTI) acknowledged that the country serves as an international trading hub, including for energy commodities such as natural gas and LNG.
 MTI noted that more than 50 Singapore-based companies currently purchase and resell these commodities to various countries, including the United States, Malaysia and Australia.
 "Although these trading companies are based in Singapore, their LNG cargoes typically move directly from the country of origin to the destination country without passing through Singapore," an MTI spokesperson said, as reported by CNA.
 Meanwhile, the MTI spokesperson said Indonesian natural gas delivered to Singapore through pipelines was used exclusively for domestic consumption and was not re-exported, contrary to Bahlil's suspicions.
 As previously reported by IDNFinancials.com, Indonesia began reducing its natural gas supplies to Singapore in the third week of October 2026. Bahlil said the move was made in accordance with President Prabowo Subianto's directive, as Indonesia had entered survival mode amid global market volatility, which has driven up energy commodity prices.
 Since the supply restrictions were introduced, LNG prices have risen by 9.24% to US$32.84 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), according to the Platts JKM spot LNG benchmark, which is used for deliveries to Japan and South Korea. (KR/LM)
